problems.quote: At the individual level, the average pairwise semantic divergence within each participant’s set of ideas was computed per condition (AI-assisted vs. unaided) and compared via a paired samples t-test.
problems.note: Null is not an allowed se_basis value. The stated method uses one average per participant and a paired test, nominally participant. However, the Results print t(364) in a study of 51 people, so the implemented independent-unit basis cannot be confirmed. The extraction already acknowledges this conflict; it remains a schema/codebook blocker rather than evidence for a guessed replacement. not_reported is also inappropriate because a t statistic, p-value and confidence interval are printed. A policy for unresolved reported units or clarification of the analysis is needed before this uncertainty can be treated as verified participant-level precision. Preserve the printed df and do not infer participant counts from it.

problems.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.1 (corpus total); PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2; PDF p. 10, Section 4.3 (group semantic test)
problems.note: The cited 728 is the number of ideas gathered for the study, not an explicitly reported analysis count for semantic divergence. The semantic paragraph gives t(728), where 728 is a degree of freedom, and does not give its own N or arm observation counts. The incompatible df leaves the implemented semantic sample unresolved, as the extraction itself notes. n_units is an analysis-observation count, so this unconfirmed corpus-to-analysis assignment should be null; retain 728 only as the separately described corpus size. Do not infer a replacement sample size from the df or borrow the category-size analysis counts.

summary: Checked all 40 estimates against the paper and the extraction rules. Read the entire 92,166-character markdown conversion through the end of References (17 PDF pages; no appendix or supplement is identified), and extracted every numerically cited PDF page: 5, 8, 9, 10 and 13. Also checked the design and measurement passages on PDF pages 4-7 and the semantic figure caption on page 11. All 167 source quotations match their exact cited pages after whitespace and invisible-format-character normalization. The 12 flagged Table 5 quotations and four flagged Table 7 difference quotations are therefore false-positive text-matching failures; their numbers, table columns and printed signs are correct. No transcribed statistic or arm descriptive value was found to differ from the PDF. There are 16 findings: eight invalid null measure codes whose valid replacements cannot be established from the paper/codebook; one invalid null se_basis with internally conflicting reported units; six after-AI records that construct an unreported contrast across tasks and periods; and one unconfirmed semantic-analysis observation count borrowed from the full corpus. The elaboration code findings identify schema/mapping gaps, not evidence of a particular unreported scoring method. The semantic signs, degrees of freedom and confidence intervals are printed as recorded; the paper’s internal inconsistencies must not be repaired by changing their signs, swapping arms or inferring counts. The 51-person crossover counts, 24/27 sequence groups and separately labelled idea counts in the other analyses were confirmed. No additional in-scope outcome or reported full-sample AI contrast was found missing. Baseline checks, process measures, order interactions and pooled task totals are appropriately outside the requested extraction scope.
